title: Line height fixed with !important
user_impact: Users cannot increase line height for readability.
technical_impact: line-height below 1.5 set with !important in a style attribute.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.12 Text Spacing (line height (line spacing) at least 1.5 times the font size); CSS Cascade 4 (author !important in a style attribute); ACT 78fd32
checks.applicability: Rendered elements with text whose style attribute sets line-height with !important to a value other than inherit, unset, revert or revert-layer.
checks.expectation:
Fails when that value is below 1.5 times the font size: an author declaration
with !important in the style attribute wins over every author style sheet,
including the one a text-spacing bookmarklet or extension injects, so the line
height (line spacing) 1.4.12 requires cannot be set. 120% fails; exactly 1.5
passes. inherit, unset and revert take over a value not fixed here and do not
count; a value without !important can be overridden and does not apply. When
layout decides whether the text is affected (the element or an ancestor is
positioned absolute/fixed, the font size a px value is compared with is not
given in px, or for line height a horizontally scrolling ancestor), the
finding is a review, not a violation. Text that is not rendered (display:
none) is out of scope. Reported once per element.
